downstream_consumers: synthesis units that must preserve contradictory evidence
question: Which venues systematically hold negative results about tooling — closed-wontfix issues, reverted commits, retracted or failed-replication papers, 'we migrated away from X' posts, deprecation notices, post-incident reviews — and what is the retrieval recipe and expected yield for each?
residual_unknowns: Failed-replication journals as a distinct index (not retractions).
wontfix totals for nodejs/node (Issues API has no total_count; search was not used for that venue to conserve the 10/min unauthenticated commit-search quota).
Whether vendor postmortems omit the worst incidents.
schema_note: Declared output_schema is research-claim-record.schema.json; that file is absent in this worktree (RES-0001 not delivered here). This document is a research-claim record by field content, not a jsonschema-validated instance.
strongest_surviving_counterargument: Blog and deprecation 'yield' is recipe-on-known-URLs, not a search-index recall estimate. A host that does not publish postmortems would look UNPRODUCTIVE under this recipe even if incidents occurred. Also, GitHub unauthenticated search totals can drift; the pinned snapshots are the measurement, not a live re-query of GitHub.
